import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ascending descending base exponent transform of squares

a n is $\sum_{i=1}^n (i^2)^((n-i+1)^2)$.

*References:*
- [A113257](https://oeis.org/A113257)
-/

namespace OeisA113257

/-- a n is the ascending descending base exponent transform of squares -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, (i ^ 2) ^ ((n - i + 1) ^ 2)

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 5 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 266 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 268722 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : a 5 = 4682453347 := by decide

/--
The smallest prime in this sequence is $a(2) = 5$. What is the next prime?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture1 :
    answer(sorry) = a (sInf {n : ℕ | 2 < n ∧ (a n).Prime}) := by
  sorry

/--
What is the first square value after 1?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture2 :
    answer(sorry) = a (sInf {n : ℕ | 1 < n ∧ IsSquare (a n)}) := by
  sorry

end OeisA113257

reformulations.difference: Computes the next prime value by applying a to the least qualifying index n > 2. If no such index exists, the expression returns 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proved StrictMono a and a 0 = 0. Consequently, a '' {n | 2 < n ∧ (a n).Prime} is exactly the set V of sequence values that are prime and greater than 5. For every q, proved q = a (sInf {n | 2 < n ∧ (a n).Prime}) ↔ ((q = 0 ∧ V = ∅) ∨ IsLeast V q). Also proved that the expression equals zero exactly when no qualifying index exists. Thus it determines the requested next prime, with an unambiguous zero encoding of nonexistence rather than an assertion that another prime must exist.

reformulations.difference: Computes the first square value after 1 by minimizing indices n > 1, then applying a; nonexistence is encoded by 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Strict monotonicity and a 1 = 1 identify a '' {n | 1 < n ∧ IsSquare (a n)} with the set V of square sequence values greater than 1. For every q, proved q = a (sInf {n | 1 < n ∧ IsSquare (a n)}) ↔ ((q = 0 ∧ V = ∅) ∨ IsLeast V q). Zero occurs exactly when there is no qualifying index, so this preserves both the least-square answer and the possible answer that no further square exists.
